mechanism_narrative: A persistently low federal funds rate compresses discount rates for equity valuation, generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as the monetary policy stance remains accommodative.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 0.25%.

mechanism_narrative: When unemployment rate exceeds 8.5%, it signals a weak labor market that suppresses consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when UNRATE > 8.5%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous weakness in housing starts (HOUST) and industrial production (INDPRO) indicates a broad-based economic slowdown, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days due to reduced corporate revenue expectations.
failure_condition: The joint signal of HOUST < 600 and INDPRO < 96 fails to predict negative returns in more than 55% of cases over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During monetary tightening cycles (FEDFUNDS > 0.5%), the Fed's policy shift increases real interest rates, reducing equity valuations and producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS > 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: Housing starts below 600 thousand units indicate weak residential demand, which correlates with reduced consumer spending and lower corporate profits, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when HOUST < 600.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of rising interest rates (FEDFUNDS) and high unemployment (UNRATE > 8.0%) signals a dual stress on the economy, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days as both monetary policy and labor market conditions deteriorate.
failure_condition: The joint signal of FEDFUNDS rising and UNRATE > 8.0% fails to predict negative returns in more than 55% of cases over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In the recession recovery phase, a rising industrial production (INDPRO) signals improving economic conditions, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days as corporate earnings growth accelerates.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO is rising during recession recovery.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in industrial production (INDPRO) reflects expanding economic output, boosting corporate profits and generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as market sentiment improves rapidly.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO is rising.
